questions.stem:
Statements: All cats are animals. All animals are living things.
Conclusions: I. All cats are living things. II. All animals are cats.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All cats are animals (UA) + All animals are living (UA) → All cats are living. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All animals are cats — not given; cannot reverse a universal affirmative. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All tigers are cats. No cat is a dog.
Conclusions: I. No tiger is a dog. II. Some dogs are tigers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All T are C (UA) + No C is D (UN) → No T is D. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'Some dogs are tigers' — contradict the valid 'No tiger is a dog'. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some books are pens. All pens are pencils.
Conclusions: I. Some books are pencils. II. All pencils are books.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: Some B are P (PA) + All P are Pc (UA) → Some B are Pc. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All pencils are books — not deducible; cannot universally reverse. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No bird is a mammal. Some mammals are pets.
Conclusions: I. Some pets are not birds. II. No pet is a bird.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: Some mammals are pets + No bird is a mammal → those mammal-pets are not birds → Some pets are not birds. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'No pet is a bird' — pets could include birds (parrots as pets) via other routes not excluded by statements. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants.
Conclusions: I. All roses are plants. II. Some plants are roses.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All R are F + All F are P → All R are P. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All R are P → by particular conversion, Some P are R. VALID ✓
Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some doctors are teachers. Some teachers are authors.
Conclusions: I. Some doctors are authors. II. Some authors are doctors.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Particular Affirmative (PA) + Particular Affirmative (PA) → No definite conclusion.
The overlap of 'doctors who are teachers' with 'teachers who are authors' is not guaranteed.
Neither I nor II follows definitively.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All scientists are intelligent. Some intelligent persons are lazy.
Conclusions: I. Some scientists are lazy. II. Some lazy persons are intelligent.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All S are I + Some I are L → Some S are L? INVALID — the lazy subset of I may not include any scientists.
Conclusion II: 'Some I are L' → by simple conversion → Some L are I. VALID ✓
Only II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some boys are tall. All tall persons are smart.
Conclusions: I. Some boys are smart. II. All smart persons are boys.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: Some B are T (PA) + All T are S (UA) → Some B are S. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'All smart are boys' — cannot reverse a UA; many smart persons may not be boys. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No apple is an orange. Some oranges are fruits.
Conclusions: I. Some fruits are not apples. II. Some apples are fruits.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: Some O are F + No A is O → Those fruit-oranges are definitely not apples → Some fruits are not apples. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'Some apples are fruits' — not given; apples may or may not be fruits per the statements. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All tables are furniture. Some furniture is wooden.
Conclusions: I. Some tables are wooden. II. Some wooden things are furniture.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All T are F + Some F are W → Some T are W? INVALID — the wooden furniture may not include any tables.
Conclusion II: 'Some F are W' → by conversion → Some W are F. VALID ✓
Only II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All A are B. No B is C.
Conclusions: I. No A is C. II. Some B are not A.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All A are B (UA) + No B is C (UN) → No A is C. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'Some B are not A' — requires B to be bigger than A, which is not stated. INVALID.
Note: 'All A are B' could mean A = B (all B are also A), so we can't say 'Some B are not A'.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some fruits are sweet. All sweet things are liked. All liked things are healthy.
Conclusions: I. Some fruits are healthy. II. All sweet things are healthy.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Chain: Some F → sweet; All sweet → liked; All liked → healthy
Conclusion I: Some F are S + All S are L → Some F are L; Some F are L + All L are H → Some F are H. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All S are L + All L are H → All S are H. VALID ✓
Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All players are athletes. All athletes are fit. Some fit persons are young.
Conclusions: I. All players are fit. II. Some players are young.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All P are A + All A are F → All P are F. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All P are F + Some F are Y → Some P are Y? INVALID — 'Some F are Y' doesn't guarantee the Y-subset overlaps with P.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No poor person is happy. All beggars are poor.
Conclusions: I. No beggar is happy. II. Some poor persons are beggars.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All B are P + No P is H → No B is H. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All B are P → by conversion (assuming beggars exist) Some P are B. VALID ✓
Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some artists are musicians. No musician is a dancer.
Conclusions: I. Some artists are not dancers. II. No artist is a dancer.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: Some A are M + No M is D → Those artist-musicians are not dancers → Some A are not D. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'No artist is a dancer' — artists who are NOT musicians could still be dancers. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All pens write. All writing is art. No art is digital.
Conclusions: I. No pen is digital. II. Some pens are art.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All P are W + All W are A → All P are A; All P are A + No A is D → No P is D. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All P are W + All W are A → All P are A → Some P are A (particular follows from universal). VALID ✓
Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All managers are executives. Some executives are graduates. All graduates are experienced.
Conclusions: I. Some managers are graduates. II. Some executives are experienced.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All M are E + Some E are G → Some M are G? INVALID — the graduate executives may not overlap with manager-executives.
Conclusion II: Some E are G + All G are Ex → Some E are Ex. VALID ✓
Only II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: No square is a circle. Some circles are ovals. All ovals are shapes.
Conclusions: I. No square is an oval. II. Some shapes are circles.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: 'No square is an oval' — ovals that are not circles could be squares; the given statements don't prevent this. INVALID.
Conclusion II: Some C are O + All O are Sh → Some C are Sh → Some Sh are C (by conversion). VALID ✓
Only II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All students are readers. All readers are thinkers. No thinker is idle.
Conclusions: I. No student is idle. II. All thinkers are students.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All S → R → T → No T is idle → No S is idle. Chain: All S are T + No T is I → No S is I. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'All thinkers are students' — cannot reverse the chain; readers and others may be thinkers too. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All lions are tigers. All tigers are cats. No cat is a dog.
Conclusions: I. No lion is a dog. II. Some cats are lions.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All L are T + All T are C → All L are C; All L are C + No C is D → No L is D. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All L are C → by conversion Some C are L (since lions exist as a subset of cats). VALID ✓
Both follow.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some students fail. All who fail are disappointed. All disappointed are depressed.
Conclusions: I. Some students are depressed. II. All depressed are students.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: Some S → fail → disappointed → depressed chain: Some S fail + All fail → disappointed → Some S disappointed; + All disappointed → depressed → Some S depressed. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'All depressed are students' — non-students can also fail, be disappointed and depressed. INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All birds fly. Some flying things are machines. No machine is alive.
Conclusions: I. Some birds are machines. II. Some flying things are not alive.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All B are F + Some F are M → Some B are M? INVALID — the machine-flyers may not include birds.
Conclusion II: Some F are M + No M is A → Some F are not A. VALID ✓
Only II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All grapes are fruits. All fruits are sweet. No sweet thing is sour.
Conclusions: I. No grape is sour. II. All sweet things are fruits.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: All G → F → Sweet → Not sour. Chain: All G are S + No S is sour → No G is sour. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: 'All sweet things are fruits' — sweet things could include non-fruit items (candy, etc.). INVALID.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: All politicians are leaders. Some leaders are corrupt. No corrupt person is trusted.
Conclusions: I. Some politicians are not trusted. II. Some leaders are not trusted.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion II: Some L are C + No C is T → Some L are not T. VALID ✓
Conclusion I: All P are L + Some L are C — the corrupt leaders may not be politicians. INVALID (cannot chain All+Some when 'Some' is on the right).
Only II follows.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem:
Statements: Some writers are poets. All poets are creative. All creative persons are free thinkers.
Conclusions: I. Some writers are free thinkers. II. All poets are free thinkers.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
Conclusion I: Some W are P (PA) + All P are C (UA) → Some W are C; Some W are C + All C are FT → Some W are FT. VALID ✓
Conclusion II: All P are C + All C are FT → All P are FT. VALID ✓
Both follow.
